sentence: Please help the person carrying two heavy bags.
setupText: Choose the person described.
taskText: Please help the person carrying two heavy bags.
text: Choose the person described. Please help the person carrying two heavy bags.
options: The person holding and moving two bags
The person looking for a bag
answer: The person holding and moving two bags
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2881:A short carrying phrase identifies a person
explanation: Carrying two heavy bags means holding the bags while moving with them.

rationales.The person buying two bags: Carrying describes holding and moving the bags, not buying them.
rationales.The person holding and moving two bags: Carrying two heavy bags means holding the bags while moving with them.
rationales.The person selling heavy bags: Selling bags is a different action from carrying them.
rationales.The person looking for a bag: The person described already has two bags and is not looking for one.

sentence: The woman talking to the clerk is my sister.
setupText: Choose who is speaking to the clerk.
taskText: The woman talking to the clerk is my sister.
text: Choose who is speaking to the clerk. The woman talking to the clerk is my sister.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2882:Connecting an action phrase to a family identity
explanation: Talking to the clerk describes the woman, and my sister tells us who she is.

rationales.The speaker's mother: My sister, not my mother, identifies the woman.
rationales.The clerk's sister: My belongs to the person saying the sentence, not the clerk.
rationales.The speaker's sister: Talking to the clerk describes the woman, and my sister tells us who she is.
rationales.The speaker: The speaker identifies another person as my sister; the speaker is not the woman described.

sentence: The cups made of glass are on the top shelf.
setupText: Choose the material named in the description.
taskText: The cups made of glass are on the top shelf.
text: Choose the material named in the description. The cups made of glass are on the top shelf.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2883:Made of introduces a material description
explanation: Made of glass describes the cups' material.

rationales.Glass: Made of glass describes the cups' material.
rationales.Wood: Wood is a different material; the description says glass.
rationales.Paper: Paper cups are not the glass cups identified here.
rationales.Metal: Metal is not the material named after made of.

sentence: The keys left on the kitchen table are yours.
setupText: Choose where to look for the keys.
taskText: The keys left on the kitchen table are yours.
text: Choose where to look for the keys. The keys left on the kitchen table are yours.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2884:A left-on phrase identifies an object's location
explanation: Left on the kitchen table describes where someone put the keys.

rationales.Inside the kitchen cupboard: The description gives the table, not the cupboard, as the keys' location.
rationales.Under the kitchen table: On means on top of the table, not underneath it.
rationales.Beside the kitchen door: The door is not the place named in left on the kitchen table.
rationales.On the kitchen table: Left on the kitchen table describes where someone put the keys.

sentence: I heard water running into the sink.
setupText: Choose what the description tells you about the water.
taskText: I heard water running into the sink.
text: Choose what the description tells you about the water. I heard water running into the sink.
options: Water was flowing into the sink.
Water was waiting in a closed bottle.
answer: Water was flowing into the sink.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2885:An ing phrase describes the sound-producing action heard
explanation: Water running means water flowing; into the sink tells us where it was going.

Water running means water flowing; into the sink tells us where it was going.
Flowing water is present, so this does not describe a tap with no water.
The water was moving into the sink, not stored in a bottle.

sentence: Please use the door marked EXIT.
setupText: Choose the door named in the instruction.
taskText: Please use the door marked EXIT.
text: Choose the door named in the instruction. Please use the door marked EXIT.
options: The door beside the sign SHOP
The door with the sign EXIT
The door with the sign OFFICE
answer: The door with the sign EXIT
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2886:Marked plus a label describes an object
explanation: Marked EXIT is a short way to describe a door carrying that label.

rationales.The door beside the sign SHOP: SHOP names a shop entrance, not the exit identified in the instruction.
rationales.The door with no sign: Marked EXIT means that a sign or label is present.
rationales.The door with the sign EXIT: Marked EXIT is a short way to describe a door carrying that label.
rationales.The door with the sign OFFICE: OFFICE is a different label from EXIT.

sentence: The two people waiting outside ___ cold.
setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
taskText: The two people waiting outside ___ cold.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. The two people waiting outside ___ cold.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2887:A main verb follows a descriptive ing phrase
explanation: Two people is plural, so the main verb is are; waiting outside describes those people.

rationales.are: Two people is plural, so the main verb is are; waiting outside describes those people.
rationales.is: Is goes with a singular subject, but two people is plural.
rationales.am: Am is used with I, not with two people.
rationales.be: Be alone does not make this present-tense statement; use are.

sentence: The food cooked this morning is in the fridge.
setupText: Choose when the food was cooked.
taskText: The food cooked this morning is in the fridge.
text: Choose when the food was cooked. The food cooked this morning is in the fridge.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2888:Time inside a short cooked phrase
explanation: This morning belongs to cooked and gives the preparation time.

rationales.Yesterday evening: The cooking time is this morning, not yesterday evening.
rationales.Tomorrow morning: Cooked describes food already prepared, and this morning is not tomorrow.
rationales.After lunch today: After lunch is later than the morning named in the description.
rationales.This morning: This morning belongs to cooked and gives the preparation time.

sentence: A notice says to you: 'Before leaving, close the window.'
setupText: Choose who must close the window.
taskText: A notice says to you: 'Before leaving, close the window.'
text: Choose who must close the window. A notice says to you: 'Before leaving, close the window.'
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2889:The reader is the understood subject of before leaving
explanation: The command close is addressed to you; before leaving refers to your departure.

rationales.The next visitor: The notice addresses you, not a visitor arriving later.
rationales.You: The command close is addressed to you; before leaving refers to your departure.
rationales.The person outside: No person outside is given responsibility in the notice.
rationales.The last person to arrive: The instruction concerns the reader leaving, not whoever arrived last.

sentence: While cooking, keep the kitchen door open.
setupText: Choose when the instruction applies.
taskText: While cooking, keep the kitchen door open.
text: Choose when the instruction applies. While cooking, keep the kitchen door open.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2890:While plus ing expresses the time during an activity
explanation: While cooking means during the time you are cooking.

rationales.Before you buy the food: While links the instruction to cooking, not shopping beforehand.
rationales.After you finish eating: After eating is later than the activity named in while cooking.
rationales.During cooking: While cooking means during the time you are cooking.
rationales.After you close the kitchen: The instruction says to keep the door open during cooking, not wait until the kitchen closes.

sentence: The man holding a map is waiting for a bus.
setupText: Choose what the man is holding.
taskText: The man holding a map is waiting for a bus.
text: Choose what the man is holding. The man holding a map is waiting for a bus.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2891:The object of a short holding phrase
explanation: A map is the object after holding; a bus belongs to waiting for.

rationales.A bus ticket: The description names a map, not a ticket, as the object in his hands.
rationales.A phone: Holding a map does not describe holding a phone.
rationales.A map: A map is the object after holding; a bus belongs to waiting for.
rationales.A newspaper: A newspaper is a different object from the map named in the description.

sentence: Leo has a raincoat on. Complete: Leo is the man ___ by the door.
setupText: Choose the words that describe Leo's clothing now.
taskText: Leo has a raincoat on. Complete: Leo is the man ___ by the door.
text: Choose the words that describe Leo's clothing now. Leo has a raincoat on. Complete: Leo is the man ___ by the door.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2892:Choosing an ing description by its action meaning
explanation: Wearing a raincoat means that the coat is on Leo now.

rationales.buying a raincoat: Buying tells us about a purchase, not what Leo has on.
rationales.washing a raincoat: Washing describes cleaning the coat, not wearing it.
rationales.selling a raincoat: Selling describes offering the coat to someone else, not having it on.
rationales.wearing a raincoat: Wearing a raincoat means that the coat is on Leo now.

sentence: I need someone to help me move this chair.
setupText: Choose the meaning of the request.
taskText: I need someone to help me move this chair.
text: Choose the meaning of the request. I need someone to help me move this chair.
options: The speaker wants a different chair.
The speaker is helping someone sit.
The speaker has finished moving the chair.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2893:Someone to help describes a needed person
explanation: Someone to help describes the person the speaker needs.

Someone to help describes the person the speaker needs.
The chair is the thing to move; the request is for help, not a replacement chair.
The speaker wants to receive help moving the chair, not help someone sit down.
rationales.The speaker has finished moving the chai: Need someone to help describes a task still needing help, not a completed move.

sentence: Is there a place to sit near the entrance?
setupText: Choose what the visitor is looking for.
taskText: Is there a place to sit near the entrance?
text: Choose what the visitor is looking for. Is there a place to sit near the entrance?
options: A place to buy a ticket
A person sitting at the entrance
A place where a person can sit
answer: A place where a person can sit
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2894:A place to sit describes a possible use
explanation: A place to sit means a place suitable for someone to sit down.

rationales.A place to buy a ticket: To sit names sitting as the use of the place, not buying tickets.
rationales.A place where a person can sit: A place to sit means a place suitable for someone to sit down.
rationales.A person sitting at the entrance: The question asks for an available place, not a person already sitting there.
rationales.A sign showing the exit: A sign may give directions, but it is not the place to sit that the visitor requests.

sentence: After eating, put your plate in the sink.
setupText: Choose the order of the two actions.
taskText: After eating, put your plate in the sink.
text: Choose the order of the two actions. After eating, put your plate in the sink.
options: Put the plate away, then eat.
Finish eating, then move the plate.
answer: Finish eating, then move the plate.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2895:After plus ing orders a completed activity and a command
explanation: After eating means once you have eaten; putting the plate in the sink comes next.

After eating puts eating before moving the plate, not after it.
After describes one action following another, not two actions happening together.
After eating means once you have eaten; putting the plate in the sink comes next.
The instruction asks you to move the plate after eating, not wash it beforehand.

sentence: The lunch included in the price is served at noon.
setupText: Choose what is included in the price.
taskText: The lunch included in the price is served at noon.
text: Choose what is included in the price. The lunch included in the price is served at noon.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2896:Included in the price identifies a covered item
explanation: Included in the price describes lunch; at noon gives its serving time.

rationales.Dinner: Dinner is a different meal from lunch.
rationales.Breakfast: Breakfast is not the meal named in the sentence.
rationales.A drink only: The sentence includes lunch, not just a drink, in the price.
rationales.Lunch: Included in the price describes lunch; at noon gives its serving time.

sentence: The table by the window is free.
setupText: Choose the meaning of the short description.
taskText: The table by the window is free.
text: Choose the meaning of the short description. The table by the window is free.
options: The window beside the table is open.
The table is outside the window.
The table has no window beside it.
The table near the window is available.
answer: The table near the window is available.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2897:A phrase without a verb describes a noun's location
explanation: By the window describes the table's location, and free means available here.

By the window describes the table's location, and free means available here.
The sentence says the table is free; it does not say the window is open.
By means beside or near, not outside through the window.
By the window places the table near a window, not away from one.

sentence: Please wait here with the door open.
setupText: Choose the state of the door in the request.
taskText: Please wait here with the door open.
text: Choose the state of the door in the request. Please wait here with the door open.
options: Close the door while you wait.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2898:With plus noun and adjective describes an accompanying state
explanation: The door is to remain open while you wait here.

With the door open asks for an open door, not a closed one.
The door is to remain open while you wait here.
Locked does not describe the open state requested.
The door should be open during the wait, not opened afterward.

sentence: People not buying tickets can use the other entrance.
setupText: Choose the longer phrase with the same meaning as 'not buying tickets'.
taskText: People not buying tickets can use the other entrance.
text: Choose the longer phrase with the same meaning as 'not buying tickets'. People not buying tickets can use the other entrance.
options: who plan to buy extra tickets
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2899:Not before an ing description makes it negative
explanation: 'Not buying' is a short version of "who aren't buying" in this description.

rationales.who aren't selling tickets: 'Not selling' changes the activity from buying to selling.
rationales.who have already bought tickets: 'Already bought' reports a completed purchase; 'not buying' does not tell us that a purchase happened earlier.
rationales.who aren't buying tickets: 'Not buying' is a short version of "who aren't buying" in this description.
rationales.who plan to buy extra tickets: 'Planning to buy extra tickets' introduces a future plan that the negative description does not state.

sentence: When ready, press the green button.
setupText: Choose the full meaning of the short request.
taskText: When ready, press the green button.
text: Choose the full meaning of the short request. When ready, press the green button.
options: Press the button before it is ready.
Wait until the button turns red.
Press the button while getting ready.
Press the green button when you are ready.
answer: Press the green button when you are ready.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-a1-2900:Recovering you are from when ready in an instruction
explanation: When ready is short for when you are ready in this instruction addressed to you.

The understood person getting ready is you, and when does not mean before.
The request names the green button and says nothing about waiting for red.
When ready places readiness before the action, not partway through getting ready.
rationales.Press the green button when you are read: When ready is short for when you are ready in this instruction addressed to you.
